text:
maria: Quick sync — proposing an "ownership gardening" approach for tenant-facing surface to pay down shared-sidecar tech debt. Sketch below, want quick feedback before an RFC.

jon: TL;DR?

maria: Split the big session-mesh into two runtime pieces: a lightweight tenant-adapter (per-tenant surface, manages prefix/KV cache) + session-core (hot path, no global locks). Move tenant-specific caching out of the global sidecar. Cutover per-cohort over weeks.

kevin: That sounds promising. Perf tradeoffs? extra hop costs?

maria: Expect small cold-path increase (~1–3ms p50, p95 +5–8ms) but much better tail under contention. Core gains from removing global locks/GC churn. We'll validate with traces and replayed traffic.

sara: What about shared cache data & eviction semantics across tenants?

maria: Two-phase migration:
(1) Read-through: tenant-adapter becomes authoritative for that tenant; session-core still does fallback reads to global cache.
(2) Cutover: after 2 weeks and gating metrics, session-core stops global reads for cohort.
We'll keep eviction semantics per-tenant; adapters own their TTLs.

infra-bot: /cohort create tenant-garden-1 — cohort created (provisional)

jon: Rollout gating — what metrics + thresholds?

maria: Gate on: service_latency_p95, cache_miss_rate, request_error_rate, and quality regressions on our evals. If p95 > +10% or errors > +1% absolute, trigger rollback. Also watch token-cost delta.

kevin: More services = more SLO surfaces. How to avoid ops burden?

maria: Adapters are lightweight and colocated with existing sidecars; reuse autoscaling and observability stacks. We add a single tenant-adapter binary (same team owns it) and a small shim in session-core to preserve protocol. No new infra primitives.

sara: Any schema or DB changes?

maria: No DB migration. We'll add tenant-prefixed keys only (no structural changes). Migration helper:

```
# quick migration helper (one-off)
./tools/migrate_tenant_prefix.sh --tenant $TENANT --dry-run
```

kevin: Tests & canaries?

maria: Staging e2e with per-tenant load replay. Prod canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback hooks. Add short perf window during low-traffic hours for the 10% step.

jon: Who writes the RFC and owns follow-ups?

maria: @kevin to draft the RFC, @sara and @jon to review. I'll own perf analysis and coordinate infra cohort creation.

sara: Add a short section in the RFC about cost impact and metrics retention. We need token-level cost projection for the adapters.

kevin: :eyes: will start draft today.

maria: I'll also add a recurring "gardening" ticket in the modularization epic so we iterate on other shared services (one small extract per sprint).

jon: Add runbook hooks in the cutover doc (rollback commands, alert thresholds).

maria: Action items:
- kevin: RFC draft by EOD Fri
- sara: eviction-policy proposal and cost estimate by Mon
- jon: schedule perf window for Tue 10–11am PT
- maria: create cohort and add canary alerts

infra-bot: cohort tenant-garden-1 created (id: cg-174567)

kevin: +1 to RFC ownership, will ping arch-reviewers when draft ready.

sara: +1 from me, will add the eviction policy doc to the RFC PR.

maria: Thanks — I'll kick off the initial perf replays and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
